title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(藤本太郎研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Fujimoto Taro)
keywords: Capability for problem-setting 2.Collaborative problem-solving 3.Capability for Innovation creation 4.Capability for Implementation and objective assessment 5.Research communication skills
educationalGoal: This course develops team-based real-world problem-solving skills by engaging students in a structured process that includes problem formulation, team-based solution development and implementation, empirical evaluation, and presentation with feedback.
advice: This course addresses societal challenges and new business creation by focusing on digital solutions leveraging IT and AI (DX: Digital Transformation). Students learn methods for collaboratively developing innovative DX-based solutions to real-world problems. With a primary focus on the smart city domain, students experience an end-to-end process of problem definition, innovation creation, implementation, empirical evaluation, and presentation through the following technical areas: 1. Integrated control of housing equipment and home appliances (Physical AI) 2. Sensing and feedback using cameras and various sensors (IoT) 3. Context-aware natural language processing 4. Web3 technologies (metaverse, NFTs) 5. Behavior analysis
requiredKnowledge: (a) A strong interest in artificial intelligence and information engineering technologies (b) A strong interest in social trends where IT and AI are applied (c) A positive attitude toward hands-on technical and programming activities

activityGoals.body: Establish an overall research plan and define achievable goals within a one-year timeframe for the goal.
Design and plan concrete research and development processes based on the self-defined research theme.
Appropriately investigate, organize, and synthesize specialized knowledge in information engineering and AI.
Identify and appropriately address various issues that arise during the research process.
Technical and objective evaluations of their research outcomes based on prior studies and current situation.
Explain the research outcomes to others in a manner.
